label: Institution
name: Bashkir State Art Museum (Nesterov Museum)
summary:
The Bashkir State Art Museum (also known as the Nesterov Museum, Russian: Башкирский государственный художественный музей имени М.В. Нестерова) in Ufa, Russia — the Republic of Bashkortostan's premier art museum, named for Mikhail Nesterov (1862-1942), the Russian religious and landscape painter born in Ufa — houses an exceptional collection of Russian and Bashkir art, including the largest collection of Nesterov's original works, alongside significant Russian imperial and Soviet art.

Mikhail Nesterov is one of the most important Russian painters of the late 19th-early 20th century, known for his deeply spiritual religious paintings (particularly 'The Vision of the Youth Bartholomew,' 1890, depicting the mystical vision of the young boy who would become Saint Sergius of Radonezh) and his landscape paintings of the Russian forest and religious communities. His work combined the Russian landscape tradition with deep Orthodox Christian mysticism, earning him the sobriquet 'painter of the Russian soul.'

The Nesterov Museum holds the world's largest collection of Nesterov's paintings — given that the artist was from Ufa and donated works to his hometown museum — making it an essential destination for scholars of Russian religious art. The collection includes the full range of Nesterov's career from early realistic paintings through his mystical religious work to his late Soviet-era portraits. The museum's comprehensive Bashkir and Russian art collection makes it the Volga-Ural region's most important art institution.
